valueProp.headline: Built for healthspan, not just fitness.
valueProp.subheadline: Healthspan is how long you live in good health — not just how long you live. Pulse keeps you consistent on the few habits that actually move it forward.

bigMovers.headline: The big movers for healthspan
bigMovers.subheadline: Three habits do most of the work for the years you live in good health. Pulse shows the trend on each, so consistency becomes visible.

movers.title: Cardio fitness
movers.description: Cardiorespiratory fitness is the single strongest predictor of healthspan. Pulse charts your VO2max and Fitness Age over time so you can see whether your training is actually moving the metric that matters most — not just logging miles.

movers.title: Strength training
movers.description: Strength is the second-largest lever — and the easiest one to drift on. Pulse counts your strength sessions and surfaces consistency week over week so the gym habit doesn't quietly disappear from your calendar.

movers.title: Recovery & sleep
movers.description: How well you recover and sleep is what lets the training compound. Pulse turns nightly HRV and sleep stages into a baseline-relative trend, so you spot drift before it costs you a workout.

howItWorks.headline: Three steps from sign-up to insight

steps.title: Connect your Garmin
steps.description: One-tap OAuth with Garmin Connect. No new device, no syncing dance, no extra wearable on your wrist.

steps.title: We pull your last 30 days
steps.description: Pulse imports your Body Battery, HRV, sleep stages, and training load history so the app is useful from day one.

steps.title: Open Pulse every morning
steps.description: Recovery, strain, and sleep on the home screen — distilled from your Garmin into the one view you'll actually check.

features.headline: Your Garmin data, finally working for you

items.title: Recovery, surfaced
items.description: Body Battery, HRV, and sleep distilled into a single recovery score on the home screen — not buried five taps deep.

items.title: Strain that means something
items.description: Today's training load against your recommended target. A clear answer to 'should I push hard or back off?' — not a raw number.

items.title: Sleep clarity
items.description: Stages, sleep debt, and last night versus your personal baseline. See drift before it costs you a workout.

items.title: No new hardware
items.description: Works with every Garmin watch that reports HRV and sleep — Forerunner, Fenix, Epix, Venu, Vivoactive. Wear what you already wear.

items.title: Trends, not snapshots
items.description: Your last 30 / 90 / 365 days of recovery and strain on one chart. Spot the patterns a daily widget can't show you.

items.title: Your data, your control
items.description: Read-only Garmin OAuth. Export or delete everything in one click. No third-party sharing. Ever.

timeline.headline: What to expect in your first weeks

steps.title: Day 1 — Connect and see your last 30 days
steps.description: One-tap Garmin OAuth and Pulse imports a month of recovery, strain, and sleep history. The app is useful from the first morning, not after a waiting period.

steps.title: Days 2–7 — The morning check-in becomes routine
steps.description: Pulse syncs nightly. You start spotting the pattern between your strain target and how you feel the next day. Sleep debt and Body Battery drift become visible signals, not background noise.

steps.title: Week 2 — Pulse learns your personal baseline
steps.description: HRV varies a lot person-to-person, so 'recovered' has to be defined relative to your normal — not a population average. Pulse begins building your baseline so the recovery score reflects your body, not a generic curve.

steps.title: Week 3 and beyond — Your recovery score sharpens
steps.description: Once your baseline locks in, daily recovery becomes a meaningful signal: a green day really is a push day, a red day really is a back-off day. The longer you wear your Garmin, the smarter Pulse gets.

items.question: What's included with my Pulse membership?
items.answer: Recovery, strain, and sleep tracking from your Garmin. AI-powered trends across 30, 90, and 365 days. 30 days of history available the moment you connect — no waiting period to get value. New features ship continuously, included in your subscription.

items.question: Which Garmin watches work with Pulse?
items.answer: Any Garmin watch that reports HRV and sleep through Garmin Connect — Forerunner 245 and newer, Fenix 6 and newer, Epix, Venu 2 and newer, Vivoactive 4 and newer, Enduro, MARQ. If your watch shows Body Battery and HRV Status in Garmin Connect today, Pulse works with it.

items.question: How does my Garmin data get to Pulse?
items.answer: A one-time, read-only OAuth connection with Garmin Connect. Pulse pulls your Body Battery, HRV, sleep stages, and training load through Garmin's official Health API. We never modify, write to, or remove anything from Garmin Connect — read-only means read-only.

items.question: Will Pulse drain my watch battery?
items.answer: No. Pulse reads data your Garmin already collects on its normal schedule. Nothing changes on the watch itself. Your 14+ day battery life is unchanged.

items.question: How does the 7-day free trial work?
items.answer: Sign up, connect your Garmin, and use Pulse with full access for 7 days. We charge $9.99/mo only if you keep it past the trial. Cancel any time in the app — no email, no phone call, no questions.

items.question: What if I cancel — do I lose my data?
items.answer: You keep full access through the end of your billing period, then your account pauses. Your history stays intact — reactivate any time and it all returns. Want it gone for good? One click in account settings deletes everything permanently.

items.question: Is my data private?
items.answer: Always. Read-only Garmin OAuth, never sold, never shared with third parties. Export everything to CSV or PDF in one click. Delete everything in one click. Your health data is yours.

items.question: Is there an annual plan?
items.answer: Yes — $79/year, which works out to ~$6.60/mo (a 33% discount on monthly). You can switch to annual on the trial-end screen or any time in account settings.
